identity.title: Information Flow Reveals When to Trust Language Models

problem.claim: Assess whether retrieval-augmented language-model predictions are contextually grounded and therefore reliable.

gap.claim: Existing uncertainty-quantification methods examine only a few layers and miss progressive information propagation, limiting their capture of grounding dynamics.

contributions.claim: Uses information flow to construct a layer-wise trace of each context token’s contribution to the output.
Introduces simulatability and concentration to calibrate prediction confidence from token-level contribution patterns.

stated_novelty.claim: The approach provides an interpretable, whole-propagation trace for grounding assessment and derives two confidence measures from it.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report an average AUROC of 0.709, compared with 0.676 for the runner-up, at moderate computational cost.

narrative_sequence.summary: Retrieval-augmented models may answer incorrectly when they fail to use query-relevant retrieved content.
The abstract shifts uncertainty quantification toward measuring contextual grounding in query-relevant tokens.
Prior methods are described as overlooking progressive information propagation across the model.
Information flow yields a layer-wise token-contribution trace, followed by simulatability and concentration measures.
Experiments are reported to achieve 0.709 average AUROC versus 0.676 for the runner-up, with moderate computational cost.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links specific contribution patterns—alignment with true relevance and concentration on a focused token subset—to prediction correctness.

lessons.interpretation: A method’s interpretability signals can be turned into explicit, testable confidence criteria.
lessons.application: Define confidence features from interpretable internal signals and state the behavioral condition each feature is intended to represent.
lessons.exception: This move is unsuitable when the proposed internal signal lacks an observable relevance target or cannot be evaluated against outcomes.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, baselines beyond the runner-up, uncertainty-calibration protocol, or how computational cost is measured.
It does not report separate results for simulatability and concentration or establish which signal drives the aggregate AUROC.
